I found no paper testing this exact GRU4Rec gate together with all the proposed controls. Closest conceptual support: [Pourzanjani et al., Improving the Identifiability of Neural Networks for Bayesian Inference](https://cse.cs.ucsb.edu/sites/default/files/publications/nips_.pdf) analyzes compensating weight scalings; [Kobayashi et al., Attention Is Not Only a Weight](https://aclanthology.org/2020.emnlp-main.574/) shows why scalar weights must be interpreted alongside transformed-vector norms. Applied here, gate magnitude alone cannot measure text contribution: W and token-embedding scales can compensate. This is an analogy, not proof of arbitrary exact rescaling of a frequency-dependent sigmoid. Additionally, unrestricted ID embeddings can absorb changes in the additive text residual, making the decomposition nonunique.

Closest recommendation evidence: [Are Multimodal Embeddings Truly Beneficial for Recommendation?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07399) replaces modality embeddings with constants/noise while preserving architecture, addressing capacity-confounded ablations. [Malitesta et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.12911) finds that individual modalities can amplify popularity bias on Amazon datasets. Neither establishes the complete requested diagnostic protocol.

A defensible extension would report ||g_i W mean(tokens_i)||/(||ID_i||+ε), branch alignment, and validation effects by training-frequency bin; norms describe representation magnitude, not causal usefulness. Compare separately retrained single GRU4Rec models using learned versus fixed gates, parameter-matched ID-only capacity, and item-text mappings shuffled within training-frequency bins. Such shuffling approximately preserves frequency structure while disrupting item-specific alignment. Distinguish retraining controls from inference-only interventions, which measure reliance but can introduce distribution shift. These are proposed controls synthesized from the literature, not published findings for this exact architecture.
